analysis: What changed versus the 4:00 AM brief: the morning's big pending item landed — USAC reported Q3 before the open (see usac), and the pre-bell earnings wave widened to Pfizer, Shopify, Marathon Petroleum and ADM. Futures drifted lower on the Dow and S&P from the 4:00 AM snapshot while the Nasdaq held a small gain, the same split tape: election-day de-risking hitting blue chips while chips stabilize. The 'beats get punished' theme held selectively: Shopify beat on adjusted EPS and grew revenue 32%, yet sank ~19% premarket on a GMV miss and a revenue print just shy of estimates; Pfizer beat and raised guidance and ticked up only ~0.6%. Apple detail deepened overnight — the September 47.9% gross margin included about 1 point of tariff refunds, so the ex-refund margin was ~46.9%, making the 45-46% December guide a smaller but still real step-down, with memory costs and Siri ramp both weighing and Mac/iPad supply constrained in the December quarter. Oil's rebound extended (Brent up again after Monday's ~8% slide), and Barron's live blog notes CME FedWatch pricing a 72% chance of a 25bp December hike — a hawkish wrinkle into Friday's payrolls. Signal vs noise: USAC's print is signal for this brief's own name (revenue beat, coverage up to 1.67x, FY guidance set); the Mag-7 debt figure ($578B, SBI via Inshorts) is single-source context for the AI-spending debate, not a fresh catalyst; midterm/prediction-market chatter stays noise until results land overnight.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures mixed-to-lower at 7:36 a.m. ET: Dow futures -0.69%, S&P 500 futures -0.07%, Nasdaq 100 futures +0.34% (Swingfolio); Barron's live blog similarly has Dow -0.8%, S&P -0.3%, Nasdaq +0.3%, with VIX futures +0.99%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The Dow/S&P drifted lower since the 4:00 AM snapshot while the Nasdaq held green — election-day caution in blue chips, stabilization in tech.

headlines.headline: Shopify plunged ~19% premarket to $127 after Q3: revenue $3.74B (+32% YoY, roughly matching estimates), adjusted EPS $0.49 vs $0.47 expected, but gross merchandise volume $119.1B vs ~$120B expected; Q4 revenue growth guided to the low-30% range, broadly in line with expectations (Barron's/WSJ).
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat on EPS still sold off hard on a GMV miss — the market is charging growth names for any sign the growth rate is topping out.

headlines.headline: Pfizer beat and raised guidance: Q3 revenue $16.58B vs ~$15.85B expected, adjusted EPS $0.87 vs $0.73-0.74 expected; non-COVID revenue +7% operationally, launched/acquired products +32%; FY2026 revenue guidance raised to $62-64B (from $60.5-62.5B) and adjusted EPS to $2.95-3.05 (from $2.80-3.00). Shares ticked up ~0.6% premarket (Barron's).
headlines.why_it_matters: Raised guidance plus a beat — a defensive name offering a modest offset to the tech-led caution, though the premarket gain is small.

headlines.headline: Marathon Petroleum beat big on refining margins: Q3 adjusted EPS $26.93 vs $24.47 expected (LSEG), net income $7.4B, adjusted EBITDA $11.7B vs $3.2B a year ago; refining and marketing margin $45.70/barrel vs $17.60 a year ago; dividend raised 10%; agreed to sell the St. Paul Park and Mandan refineries plus related midstream assets to CVR Energy for $4.2B.
headlines.why_it_matters: Refining margins at multi-year highs drove the beat, and selling two refineries into that strength converts a volatile earnings stream into cash.

headlines.headline: ADM beat on EPS and raised guidance: Q3 adjusted EPS $1.77 vs $1.63 Zacks consensus (vs $0.92 a year ago), revenue $22.34B missing consensus by 1.49%; FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance raised to $5.50-5.80 from $5.15-5.60.
headlines.why_it_matters: EPS beat plus a guidance raise outweighs a small revenue miss — ag processing is benefiting from the constructive biofuels backdrop management cited.

headlines.headline: Apple still down ~4% premarket, with new margin detail: the September 47.9% gross margin included about 1 percentage point of tariff refunds (about $0.05 of EPS), implying ~46.9% ex-refund; December-quarter revenue growth guided to 7-10% with Services +8-9%, gross margin 45-46% on higher memory costs and Siri AI ramp, and memory-driven supply constraints expected for Mac and iPad (Reuters/The Register).
headlines.why_it_matters: The beat was flattered by tariff refunds, so the margin step-down is real but smaller than the headline suggests — still, memory costs rising beyond December keep the pressure on.

headlines.headline: Chips held their bounce: Nvidia +1.6% after four down sessions, AMD +2.8% ahead of its after-bell print, with Marvell and Intel also higher (Reuters). Palantir remained lower after its bookings deceleration (Q3 revenue $2.313B, +96%, but total contract value +6% after +49% in Q2).
headlines.why_it_matters: Stabilization in the most beaten-down group into AMD's print — the bounce needs an earnings confirmation to become a reversal.

headlines.headline: Oil rebounded further: Brent crude futures +1.15% premarket (Barron's), after Monday's ~8% slide on diplomacy hopes reversed on reports of the U.S. strike on Iran's Qeshm Island and an Iranian official saying a deal was far off; gold futures -1.27%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The prior session's biggest tailwind keeps reversing — higher crude re-tightens the inflation headwind into the open.

headlines.headline: Midterms today, macro at 10:00 a.m. ET: September JOLTS job openings and factory orders are due at 10:00 a.m. ET; polls and analysts favor Democrats taking the House with Senate control uncertain. Barron's live blog notes CME FedWatch pricing a 72% chance of a 25bp December rate hike.
headlines.why_it_matters: Results emerge overnight, so traders carry election risk with no scheduled announcement to trade against, and a hawkish December pricing wrinkle sits ahead of Friday's payrolls.

headlines.headline: Magnificent Seven combined debt rose ~45% to $578B by mid-2026, up from $399B in 2025, per SBI Research (via Inshorts); the report warns rising Treasury yields could cut their combined market cap by $1.67-2T.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed in detail — if the debt build holds, it quantifies the AI-capex leverage behind the tech correction; treat the market-cap warning as fragile until the primary research is seen.

usac.headline: USA Compression Partners reported Q3 2026 before the open: total revenue $357.2M vs $250.3M a year ago and vs ~$348.32M consensus, net income $47.3M, diluted net income per common unit $0.33 (vs $0.31 in Q2, $0.26 a year ago), Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M vs $160.3M a year ago, Distributable Cash Flow $127.1M with coverage 1.67x (vs 1.61x a year ago); distribution held at $0.525 per unit. FY2026 guidance set at Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M. Average revenue-generating horsepower 4.48M vs 3.55M a year ago; revenue per horsepower per month $23.14 vs $21.46; average utilization 92.1% vs 94.0%. Call at 11:00 a.m. ET today (company release).
usac.why_it_matters: Revenue beat consensus, EBITDA and DCF grew both year-over-year and sequentially, coverage improved, and the distribution held — the print supports the payout into today's call, with the $0.525 distribution paying Nov 6 to holders of record Oct 26. Last reported quarter (Q2, Aug 4): EPS $0.31 beat the $0.28 consensus, revenue $342.15M vs $340.49M expected.
